ANNEX A 3.2, TabZe 1, Item ( i ) ]
OF KITAZIN CONTENT A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution Weigh accurately 200 mg of kitazin reference standard in a lOO-ml volumetric flask and make up the volume to the mark with chloroform. Take 5 ml of this solution into a 25-ml volumetric flask and add 5 ml of the internal standard solution and finally make up the volume to the mark with chloroform. A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution Weigh accurately a quantity of the sample equivalent to 200 mg of kitazin in a loo-ml volumetric flask and make up the volume to, to mark with chloroform. Take 5 ml of this solution into a 25-ml volumetric flask and add 5 ml of the internal standard solution and finally make up the volume to the mark with chloroform. A-4.4 Estimation Inject a known volume of the standard solution and the sample solution with the help of a microlitre syringe. Measure the peak areas of. the internal standard, standard and sample. A-5 CALCULATION Kitazin content, percent by mass = M ' Ai ' A3 x '
M, x A,! X A4

DETERMINATION A-I PRINCIPLE

The sample is diluted to appropriate volume with chloroform and content is determined using dibutyl phthalate or equivalent as internal standard, by gas chromatography. A-4 PROCEDURE A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution

Weigh accurately 0'1 g dibutyl phthalate in a IOO-ml volumetric flask and make up the volume to the mark with chloroform. This will give a solution containing 1 mg/ml of The solution will remain dibutyl phthalate. stable for 4 weeks if it is stored in a tightly sealed bottle under refrigeration. Allow the solution to attain room temperature before use.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed

by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained-from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
